- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:549 (hashlib.sha256(target.read_bytes()).hexdigest() inside entries())
  Problem: The _resolver_scope_state helper reads every tracked and untracked file's full content and computes SHA-256 on each call. entries() runs at least twice per attempt (capture before model invocation, check after), and a third time on verify after a scope-drift restore. On the current source repo (~1000 files) this adds roughly 30 seconds per attempt — well within the 50-minute per-attempt budget. But the cost scales linearly with checkout size, and the IS_WORKFLOW_SOURCE_REPO gate is the only thing keeping this off consumer-repo checkouts that can be 10x larger.
  Why it fails at runtime: No failure today. If the gate is ever widened or a consumer repo grows large binary assets, the per-attempt overhead could consume a meaningful fraction of the resolver's time budget. The existing cross-pollination consensus already flagged this as a NIT; confirming with the concrete call count (2-3 full scans per attempt, 6-9 across a 3-attempt loop).
  Severity: NIT
  Issue confidence: 3
